Vestigia tags 14 as 'olasz, titkosírás' (Italian with cipher): 295908, 295909, 295935, 295943, 295948, 295960, 295961, 295963, 295978, 295980, 295991, 295992, 295997, 296003; the others (295812, 295962, 295981, 294210, 294211, 294212, 294226) are plain Italian. seen.cipher: Every cipher piece outside catalogue 348 has a contemporary decipherment: interlinear over the cipher on DF 295943 and DF 295948 (seen here) and on DF 295991 and 295992 (Vestigia note 'A rejtjel megfejtése a sorok közé írva'); on a slip attached to DF 295978 ('feloldása külön papírszeleten'); as filed clear copies for DF 295960 (no. 41b), 295961 (42b), 295963 (44b), 295980 (14b), 295997 (31b) and 296003 (37b). DF 295908, 295909, 295935 and 295963 are catalogue 348's DECODE letters (R1162-R1167), and 295908 and 295935 also carry interlinear decipherments.

vetting.closed: Closed as read: every cipher piece in the DF set outside catalogue 348 carries its contemporary decipherment (interlinear, attached slip or filed clear copy, per Vestigia and seen on DF 295943 and 295948), and the remaining records are catalogue 348's own letters or clear letters.

1363.note: The National Archives of India's own Descriptive List of Secret Department Records vol. II (1776-1780) describes 1 Nov 1779 No. 8 as a clear autograph letter of 26 Oct 1779 from Bhagalpur in which the Commander-in-Chief's secretary asks J. P. Auriol for the cypher to read a letter from Goddard; the List footnotes letters that are written in cypher and has no such note here.

1363.correction: The lead's title (Governor-General and Council to Fort St George) is wrong: the piece is the Commander-in-Chief's secretary (W. Tierney in the List's OCR) to J. P. Auriol, Bhagalpur 26 Oct 1779, filed under 1 Nov 1779 No. 8.
